verdict: passed — convergence re-bind, not a fresh translation review: 178/178 keys bind to one of the two parents (159 shared, 11 branch-only, 8 main-only), 0 value changes, 0 invented keys, 0 lost keys; key set equals English and equals the parent union; ICU/placeholder parity 178/178 messages with 6 plural messages at the locale's exact CLDR categories (other); 1 comma-only structural exception(s); 0 blocker, 0 major, 0 minor, 0 nit.
method: Read the PR head and both parents from Git objects (git show), never from a checkout; no catalogue file was modified.
Split each merged file into its one-key-per-line records and attributed all 178 keys: exact line match first, then a single trailing-comma normalisation, against both parents independently.
Confirmed the merged key set equals the English key set and the union of the two parent key sets (A 170, B 167, shared 159), with no missing, extra or duplicate key.
Compared every merged value with the parent value(s) after JSON parsing: shared keys are identical in both parents, and each parent-only key equals its single parent.
Checked format invariants: tab-indented one-record-per-line JSON, LF, trailing newline, no BOM, unique keys, and exactly one optional trailing comma on the final record.

Parsed every merged and English message with @formatjs/icu-messageformat-parser 3.5.21, compared argument names, argument node types and number/date skeletons, plural category sets against Intl.PluralRules CLDR output for the locale, and companion argument references inside plural branches.

Ran parser negative controls: a dropped placeholder, renamed placeholder, changed skeleton, changed plural category set, dropped in-branch skeleton and malformed ICU each produced a finding, so the parity check is not vacuous.
Ran scripts/i18n/catalogue-union-parity.mjs against Git objects for this file (head, old-head A, base B): no key missing from either side and no value difference.
notes: Convergence re-bind only: this receipt proves provenance of bytes, not translation quality. Accuracy, idiom, register and glossary were not re-adjudicated in this round; those judgements belong to the audited parent waves.
The merge commit is a two-parent merge: 404902650f = d696dea4ec (branch) + 91aa8f5f10 (main). Every merged value is byte-identical to one of those two parents.
Key order is not globally lexicographic: the catalogue preserves each side's sorted core plus appended late keys. Ordering is not part of this rebind's binding rule.

The four comma-only line exceptions known from the preceding ui.common.updates convergence re-bind (hi, ur, vi, zh-CN; key ui.common.updates.error.version_unknown_required, each normalised from parent A) are present at this head as the same key/value rows; at this merge the record is final in the merged file, so the separator is absent where the earlier head carried one. The value bytes are unchanged and equal to parent A.

Exact parent bytes are referenced by existing receipts in i18n/receipts (see parents.A/B.exact_bytes_named_by). Those references have mixed scopes — translator records, delta/batch audits and, for ui.common.updates, the preceding convergence re-bind — so this receipt proves byte provenance, not an inherited whole-file quality verdict.
